OLE-FAC-SAT.note: High-pressure/high-temperature countercurrent hydrolysis (Colgate-Emery process, ~250°C/50 bar, no catalyst) splits CPO triglycerides into free saturated C16/C18 fatty acids plus a glycerine co-product stream.

FA-US.note: CPO is hydrolyzed (fat splitting) to crude fatty acids, then short-path/fractional vacuum distillation isolates the unsaturated oleic (C18:1) cut from the saturated fractions.

OLE-FAL-CPO.note: CPO is transesterified with methanol to fatty acid methyl esters (FAME), then hydrogenated over a copper-chromite catalyst at high pressure/temperature to reduce the ester to the C16-C18 fatty alcohol (releasing methanol for recycle).

OLE-FAL-PKO.note: Same methyl-ester hydrogenation route as long-cut fatty alcohols, but starting from PKO, whose shorter C12-C14 fatty-acid profile gives the mid-cut alcohol distribution after hydrogenation.

feedstocks: CPO/PKO blend or high-erucic rapeseed oil
OLE-FAL-C20.note: Very-long-chain (C20-C22, behenyl) alcohol is produced by the same methyl-ester hydrogenation route; commercially it is most often sourced from high-erucic-acid rapeseed oil rather than CPO/PKO, since palm oils carry only trace C20+ acids.

OLE-GLY-CRD.note: Crude glycerine (~80%) is the aqueous co-product stream recovered when CPO/PKO triglycerides are split (hydrolysis) or transesterified to make fatty acids, fatty alcohols, or FAME.

OLE-GLY-REF.note: Crude glycerine is neutralized, vacuum-distilled to remove water/salts/color bodies, and ion-exchange polished to reach refined 99.5% USP/food/pharma grade.

FOD-LEC-LIQ.note: Crude soybean oil is hydrated with water/steam, causing phospholipids (lecithin) to swell and precipitate out of the oil; the separated gum phase, dried, is liquid lecithin.

FOD-LEC-PWD.note: Liquid lecithin is washed with acetone to extract residual neutral oil, leaving a phospholipid-rich fraction that is dried/spray-dried to the powder form.

OLE-ME-FAME.note: CPO triglycerides react with methanol under NaOH/KOH catalysis to give fatty acid methyl esters (FAME) plus a glycerine co-product, the standard biodiesel/oleochemical transesterification route.

FOD-RBD-LIQ.note: CPO is degummed, bleached with activated clay to remove pigments/trace metals, and steam-deodorized under vacuum to strip free fatty acids and odor compounds — a physical/thermal refining sequence rather than a chemical synthesis.

FAT-STEA-PWD.note: Fatty acids from CPO/PKO are hydrogenated to saturate any double bonds, then fractionally distilled to isolate the C18 (stearic-rich) cut, typically as a stearic/palmitic acid blend.

FAT-ZNST-PWD.note: Stearic acid reacts with zinc oxide (or zinc sulfate solution) in a simple neutralization/double-decomposition reaction to precipitate zinc stearate, which is filtered and dried.

FAT-MGST-PWD.note: Stearic acid is neutralized with magnesium oxide/hydroxide to form magnesium stearate, precipitated and dried to a fine powder.

OLE-IPM-LIQ.note: Acid-catalyzed (typically sulfuric or a solid acid catalyst) condensation of myristic acid with isopropanol, with water removed to drive the equilibrium, gives isopropyl myristate.

OLE-CCT-LIQ.note: Glycerine is esterified with a caprylic/capric fatty-acid blend (derived from coconut/palm-kernel oil fractionation) under acid or enzymatic catalysis to give the CCT emollient triglyceride.

OLE-CEH-LIQ.note: Cetyl alcohol is esterified with 2-ethylhexanoic acid (itself an oxidation product of 2-ethylhexanol) under acid catalysis to give the light emollient ester.

OLE-ODD-LIQ.note: 2-Ethylhexanol undergoes base-catalyzed Guerbet condensation (dehydrogenation, aldol condensation, then re-hydrogenation of the resulting enal) to dimerize into the branched C16 Guerbet alcohol, octyldodecanol.

OLE-DCC-LIQ.note: 2-Ethylhexanol reacts with dimethyl carbonate under mild base/transesterification catalysis, releasing methanol, to give dicaprylyl carbonate.

OLE-C1215AB-LIQ.note: Benzoic acid (from toluene/benzene oxidation) is esterified with a C12-C15 synthetic (Ziegler alpha-olefin-derived) fatty alcohol blend under acid catalysis.

OLE-NEOD23-LIQ.note: Ethylene is oligomerized (Shell Higher Olefin Process, nickel catalyst) to C11-C12 linear alpha olefins, which are then hydroformylated with syngas (cobalt/rhodium catalyst) to aldehydes and hydrogenated to the C12-C13 synthetic detergent alcohol.

OLE-NEOD45-PWD.note: Same SHOP-then-oxo route as the C12-C13 grade, tuned to the C13-C14 alpha-olefin cut to give the C14-C15 synthetic detergent alcohol.

OLE-LINEVOL911-LIQ.note: Same route again on the shorter C8-C10 alpha-olefin cut, giving the C9-C11 plasticizer-grade alcohol used as a phthalate-free plasticizer precursor.

FAT-CAST-PWD.note: Stearic acid is neutralized with calcium hydroxide (lime) in a simple acid-base reaction to precipitate calcium stearate, filtered and dried to powder.

SUR-CAPB-LIQ.note: Coconut fatty acid (or its methyl ester) is first amidated with DMAPA to give a fatty amidoamine, then reacted with sodium monochloroacetate in a carboxymethylation (betainization) step to form cocamidopropyl betaine.

SUR-LABS-ACD.note: LAB is sulfonated with gaseous SO3 (falling-film sulfonation) or oleum to give linear alkylbenzene sulfonic acid (LABSA).

SUR-LABS-PWD.note: LABSA is neutralized with caustic soda to sodium LAS, then spray-dried to the 90% dry powder form.

SUR-LABS-S30.note: LABSA is neutralized with caustic soda and diluted with process water to a 30% active sodium LAS solution.

SUR-LABS-S60.note: Same LABSA neutralization as the 30% grade, run at lower dilution and elevated temperature to give a pumpable 60% active slurry.

SUR-AES-2EO.note: C12-C14 fatty alcohol is ethoxylated with ~2 moles ethylene oxide (base catalysis), then the ethoxylate is sulfated with SO3 and neutralized to give sodium laureth sulfate (SLES 2EO).

SUR-AES-3EO.note: Same ethoxylation/sulfation/neutralization sequence as the 2EO grade, using ~3 moles ethylene oxide per mole alcohol for a milder, higher-foaming SLES.

SUR-SLS-PST.note: C12-C14 fatty alcohol is sulfated directly with SO3 (no ethoxylation step) and neutralized with caustic soda to give sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS) as a 30% paste.

SUR-SLS-PWD.note: Same direct sulfation/neutralization route as the SLS paste, followed by spray drying to the 93% powder/needle form.

SUR-FAM-C12.note: PKO-derived C12-C14 fatty acids react with ammonia (via the ammonium soap) and are dehydrated to fatty nitriles, which are then catalytically hydrogenated to the primary fatty amine.

SUR-FAM-C18.note: Same nitrile-route amination as the C12-C14 amine, using CPO-derived C16-C18 fatty acids as the feedstock.

SUR-APG-LIQ.note: C12-C14 fatty alcohol reacts with glucose under acid catalysis (Fischer glycosidation) to form the alkyl glucoside, with excess alcohol recycled.

F19-IMID-LIQ.note: Fatty acid reacts with DETA to form a diamide/amidoamine intermediate, which is then cyclodehydrated (water loss, high temperature) to close the five-membered imidazoline ring.

SUR-SULF-LIQ.note: A fatty alcohol ethoxylate is half-esterified with maleic anhydride, then sodium bisulfite adds across the resulting double bond (Michael-type addition) to give the sulfosuccinate anionic surfactant.

POL-PEG-LIQ.note: Ethylene oxide undergoes base-catalyzed ring-opening polymerization from a water or glycol initiator, building up the polyethylene glycol chain to the target molecular weight.

feedstocks: Sodium isethionate (from ethylene oxide + sodium bisulfite)
SUR-SCI-PWD.note: Ethylene oxide is first reacted with sodium bisulfite to give sodium isethionate, which is then esterified with coconut fatty acid (often via the acid chloride) to give sodium cocoyl isethionate.

SUR-PS80-LIQ.note: Sorbitol is acid-dehydrated to sorbitan, esterified with oleic acid to sorbitan monooleate, then ethoxylated with ethylene oxide to give the water-soluble polysorbate 80.

SUR-SMS-PWD.note: Sorbitol is dehydrated to sorbitan and directly esterified with stearic acid to give sorbitan monostearate (Span 60), the classic W/O emulsifier.

SUR-CTG-PWD.note: C16-C18 fatty alcohol reacts with glucose under acid catalysis, the same Fischer glycosidation used for alkyl polyglucosides, to give the bio-based cetearyl glucoside emulsifier.

SUR-GSSE-PWD.note: Glycerine is esterified with stearic acid to glyceryl monostearate; a portion is co-saponified with caustic soda/potash to add a small soap fraction that makes the product self-emulsifying (SE grade).

SUR-PGL4-LIQ.note: Glycerine is base-catalyzed polymerized (dehydrative etherification) to polyglycerol-4, which is then esterified with lauric acid to give the premium non-ionic emulsifier.

feedstocks: Behenyl amine (C20-C22, from behenic acid amination)
SUR-BTAC-PST.note: Behenyl amine is quaternized with methyl chloride (itself made from methanol and hydrochloric acid) to give the quaternary ammonium salt behentrimonium chloride.

feedstocks: Cetyl amine (C16 fatty alcohol + ammonia route)
SUR-CTAC-LIQ.note: Cetyl amine is quaternized with methyl chloride to give cetrimonium chloride, the commodity-grade cationic conditioning surfactant.

feedstocks: Lauric acid (coconut oil route, as acid chloride)
SUR-SLSAR-LIQ.note: Lauroyl chloride (from lauric acid) acylates sarcosine under Schotten-Baumann conditions; the product is neutralized with caustic soda to give sodium lauroyl sarcosinate.

SUR-FAE-LIQ.note: A C12-C18 fatty alcohol is ethoxylated under base catalysis (ring-opening addition of ethylene oxide) to the target degree of ethoxylation, giving the non-ionic surfactant.

SUR-NEODEO-LIQ.note: The synthetic (SHOP/oxo-derived) NEODOL alcohol backbone is ethoxylated with 7-9 moles of ethylene oxide to give the NEODOL ethoxylate surfactant.

MIN-SORBMONO-LIQ.note: Sorbitol is dehydrated to sorbitan and esterified with oleic acid to give sorbitan monooleate (Span 80), a classic W/O emulsifier used in mining flotation formulations.

RES-PA6-PEL.note: Caprolactam's seven-membered lactam ring is opened by trace water at high temperature and polymerized into linear nylon 6 chains (hydrolytic polymerization), then extruded and pelletized.

RES-PC-PEL.note: BPA reacts with phosgene (classic interfacial process) or, increasingly, with diphenyl carbonate in a melt transesterification, polycondensing to polycarbonate with loss of HCl or phenol respectively.

F20-PCE-LIQ.note: A polyethylene-glycol methacrylate macromonomer is free-radically copolymerized with methacrylic acid (or acrylic acid) to build the comb-shaped polycarboxylate ether (PCE) superplasticizer backbone.

F20-PCE-PWD.note: Same PCE copolymerization as the liquid grade, with the resulting aqueous polymer solution spray-dried to a redispersible powder.

RES-HDPE-PEL.note: Ethylene is polymerized under Ziegler-Natta or chromium (Phillips) catalysis at low pressure to give the linear, densely-packed HDPE chain structure.

RES-LDPE-PEL.note: Ethylene is polymerized via a free-radical mechanism at very high pressure (1000-3000 bar) and temperature, producing the short- and long-chain branching characteristic of LDPE.

RES-PP-PEL.note: Propylene is stereospecifically polymerized over a TiCl4-based Ziegler-Natta catalyst system, giving predominantly isotactic polypropylene.

RES-ACR-LIQ.note: Acrylic acid and MMA are copolymerized by a free-radical emulsion process in water, giving the waterborne acrylic resin dispersion.

RES-ALK-LIQ.note: CPO fatty acids are first transesterified (alcoholyzed) with pentaerythritol, then the resulting monoglyceride reacts with phthalic anhydride in a polycondensation (esterification, water removed) to build the long-oil alkyd resin.

RES-EPX-LIQ.note: BPA and epichlorohydrin react under NaOH catalysis: the phenol first etherifies epichlorohydrin's chlorine, then NaOH dehydrohalogenates the intermediate to reform the epoxide ring, building the low-molecular-weight liquid epoxy resin (EEW 182-192).

RES-EPX-SOL.reaction: Etherification + epoxide ring closure, advanced to higher MW
RES-EPX-SOL.note: Same BPA/epichlorohydrin taffy-process chemistry as the liquid grade, but run with a lower epichlorohydrin:BPA ratio (or further advanced/chain-extended) to reach the higher-molecular-weight solid resin (EEW 450-550).

RES-PET-BOT.note: PTA is directly esterified with MEG to bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate, then melt-polycondensed (antimony or titanium catalyst, vacuum, water removed) to build PET chains to bottle-grade molecular weight.

RES-PET-FIB.note: Same PTA/MEG esterification-polycondensation route as bottle-grade PET, taken to a lower target molecular weight/intrinsic viscosity suited to melt spinning into fibre.

RES-PS-PEL.note: Styrene is polymerized by a free-radical mechanism, either in bulk (continuous mass process) or suspension, to give general-purpose (GPPS) or, with dissolved rubber, high-impact (HIPS) polystyrene.

RES-PVC-PWD.reaction: Oxychlorination/direct chlorination to EDC, cracking to VCM, then suspension polymerization
RES-PVC-PWD.note: Ethylene and chlorine combine (direct chlorination and oxychlorination) to ethylene dichloride (EDC), which is thermally cracked to vinyl chloride monomer (VCM); VCM is then free-radically polymerized in aqueous suspension to PVC.

RES-ABS-PEL.note: Styrene and acrylonitrile are grafted onto a polybutadiene rubber backbone via emulsion (or mass/suspension) free-radical polymerization, giving the two-phase ABS morphology.

RES-EVA-PEL.note: Ethylene and vinyl acetate are copolymerized under the same high-pressure free-radical conditions used for LDPE, giving the flexible EVA copolymer.

RES-PA66-PEL.note: Adipic acid and HMDA first form the stoichiometric 'nylon salt,' which is then melt-polycondensed (water removed) into the alternating diacid/diamine nylon 66 polymer chain.

RES-VAERPP-PWD.note: Ethylene and VAM are emulsion-copolymerized to a VAE latex, which is then spray-dried with a protective colloid to give the redispersible polymer powder.

POL-HPMC-PWD.note: Cellulose is alkalized with NaOH (activating the hydroxyl groups), then etherified with chloromethane (methylation) and propylene oxide (hydroxypropylation) in a Williamson-type ether synthesis to give HPMC.

POL-MCC-PWD.note: Cellulose is subjected to controlled dilute-acid (HCl) hydrolysis, which preferentially attacks the amorphous regions and leaves the crystalline cellulose microfibrils that make up MCC.

RES-LLDPE-PEL.note: Ethylene is copolymerized with a small fraction of butene-1 or hexene-1 under Ziegler-Natta or metallocene catalysis, introducing the short-chain branches that define LLDPE's properties versus HDPE.

RES-UPR-LIQ.note: Maleic anhydride and phthalic anhydride are polycondensed with propylene glycol (esterification, water removed) to build the unsaturated polyester backbone, which is then dissolved in styrene as a reactive diluent/crosslinking co-monomer for later curing.

ELA-BR-BAL.note: Butadiene is polymerized in solution using a Ziegler-Natta (neodymium or cobalt) or lithium-alkyl catalyst system to build high-cis polybutadiene, coagulated and baled.

ELA-SBR-BAL.note: Butadiene and styrene are copolymerized by a free-radical emulsion process (soap/surfactant-stabilized latex), then coagulated, dried, and baled to give SBR 1502.

ELA-NBR-BAL.note: Butadiene and acrylonitrile are emulsion-copolymerized by the same free-radical route as SBR, with the ACN content (here 33-36%) set by monomer feed ratio, then coagulated and baled to NBR.

F20-SBR-LATEX.note: Same butadiene/styrene emulsion copolymerization as solid SBR, but the resulting latex is stabilized and sold as a liquid dispersion for construction/binder applications rather than coagulated into bales.

ELA-EPDM-BAL.note: Ethylene, propylene, and a small amount of a diene (ENB) are terpolymerized under Ziegler-Natta or metallocene catalysis; the diene provides the pendant unsaturation needed for sulfur vulcanization of an otherwise saturated backbone.

ELA-NEO-CHI.reaction: Chlorination to chloroprene + emulsion free-radical polymerization
ELA-NEO-CHI.note: Butadiene is chlorinated and isomerized to chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene), which is then free-radically polymerized in emulsion to polychloroprene (neoprene), coagulated to chip/bale form.

ELA-VACC-PWD.note: Aniline reacts with carbon disulfide and sulfur to form mercaptobenzothiazole (MBT), which is then condensed with an amine (e.g. cyclohexylamine for CBS) or oxidatively coupled (for MBTS) or reacted analogously with dimethylamine and further oxidized (for TMTD) to give the respective sulfur-donor vulcanization accelerator.

ELA-SBL-LIQ.note: Styrene and butadiene are emulsion-copolymerized by the same free-radical route as SBR rubber, with the resulting latex sold directly (not coagulated) as SB latex.

SOL-TOL-LIQ.note: Naphtha is catalytically reformed (platforming, Pt catalyst) to a BTX-rich reformate, from which toluene is separated by solvent extraction and fractional distillation.

SOL-XYL-LIQ.note: Same naphtha reforming route as toluene; the mixed-xylenes cut is separated from the reformate's aromatics fraction by distillation.

CLN-ETOH-IPC.note: Fermentable sugars from corn (via enzymatic starch hydrolysis) or sugarcane are fermented by yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) to ethanol, which is then distilled and denatured for the industrial-purposes (IPC) grade.

SOL-ACE-LIQ.note: Benzene is alkylated with propylene to cumene, which is air-oxidized to cumene hydroperoxide and then acid-cleaved (Hock rearrangement) to give phenol and acetone as co-products.

SOL-ETOH-IND.note: Starch from corn or wheat is enzymatically hydrolyzed to fermentable sugars, fermented by yeast to ethanol, then distilled to the 96% industrial grade.

SOL-IPA-LIQ.note: Propylene is hydrated directly over a solid acid catalyst (or indirectly via sulfuric acid esterification/hydrolysis) to give isopropanol.

SOL-MEK-LIQ.note: n-Butylenes are hydrated (acid-catalyzed) to sec-butanol, which is then catalytically dehydrogenated (zinc or copper catalyst) to methyl ethyl ketone (MEK).

MIN-MIBC-LIQ.note: Acetone self-condenses (base-catalyzed aldol) to diacetone alcohol, which is dehydrated to mesityl oxide and then catalytically hydrogenated to methyl isobutyl carbinol (MIBC), the mining flotation frother.

SOL-BUOH-LIQ.note: Propylene is hydroformylated with syngas over a cobalt or rhodium catalyst to butyraldehyde, which is then hydrogenated to n-butanol.

SOL-MPG-LIQ.note: Propylene oxide is hydrated (non-catalytic at high temperature/pressure, or acid/base catalyzed) to open the epoxide ring and give propylene glycol.

SOL-ETAC-LIQ.note: Ethanol and acetic acid are condensed under acid catalysis (Fischer esterification, water removed) to give ethyl acetate.

SOL-BUAC-LIQ.note: n-Butanol and acetic acid are condensed under acid catalysis to give butyl acetate, with water removed to drive the equilibrium.

SOL-COAL-LIQ.note: Isobutyraldehyde undergoes base-catalyzed aldol condensation and hydrogenation to a branched glycol intermediate, which is then esterified with isobutyric acid to give the Texanol/TXIB-type ester-alcohol coalescent.

SOL-NMP-LIQ.note: Gamma-butyrolactone reacts with methylamine, the amine opening the lactone ring and then recyclizing (amide condensation) to form the five-membered N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone ring.

SOL-PGMEA-LIQ.note: Propylene oxide reacts with methanol (acid or base catalyzed ring-opening) to give propylene glycol monomethyl ether (PGME), which is then esterified with acetic acid/acetic anhydride to PGMEA.

SOL-PINE-LIQ.note: Alpha-pinene from turpentine (a forestry/pulping by-product) undergoes acid-catalyzed hydration and skeletal isomerization to terpene alcohols (chiefly alpha-terpineol), the main components of pine oil.

SOL-DPG-LIQ.note: During propylene oxide hydration to propylene glycol, a fraction of the propylene glycol reacts with a second mole of propylene oxide (ring-opening) to give the dimeric dipropylene glycol as a co-product stream, which is then separated by distillation.

SOL-DMF-LIQ.note: Dimethylamine (itself made from methanol and ammonia) reacts catalytically with carbon monoxide (carbonylation) to give N,N-dimethylformamide.

F17-PQ7-LIQ.note: DADMAC (itself made from allyl chloride and dimethylamine) is free-radically copolymerized with acrylamide in aqueous solution to give the cationic conditioning polymer polyquaternium-7.

F19-DEMUL-OIL.note: Ethylene oxide and propylene oxide are added sequentially onto a polyol initiator under base catalysis (anionic ring-opening polymerization), building the defined EO/PO block structure that gives the demulsifier its oil/water interfacial activity.

SPO-PA12-PEL.note: Laurolactam — made via cyclododecatriene hydrogenation, oxidation to cyclododecanone, oxime formation, and Beckmann rearrangement to the 12-membered lactam — is ring-opened and polymerized (analogous to nylon 6) to give PA12.

SPO-MDI-POL.note: Aniline condenses with formaldehyde (acid-catalyzed) to give a mixture of diaminodiphenylmethane (MDA) and higher-functionality polymeric MDA, which is then phosgenated to convert the amine groups to isocyanate groups, yielding polymeric MDI (PMDI).

SPO-MDI-PUR.note: Same aniline-formaldehyde condensation and phosgenation route as PMDI, with the process tuned/distilled to isolate the pure difunctional 4,4'-MDI monomer rather than the polymeric mixture.

SPO-TDI-LIQ.note: Toluene is dinitrated with nitric acid to dinitrotoluene, hydrogenated to toluenediamine (TDA), and then phosgenated to convert the amine groups to isocyanates, giving the 80/20 isomer blend of TDI.

F17-MF-CAPS.reaction: Methylolation + polycondensation (interfacial, around an oil core)
F17-MF-CAPS.note: Melamine and formaldehyde first form methylolmelamine, which polycondenses at an oil-in-water droplet interface to build a crosslinked melamine-formaldehyde shell around the oil core, forming the microcapsule.

SPO-PEEK-PEL.note: Hydroquinone's phenolate (generated with a base such as K2CO3) displaces fluoride from 4,4'-difluorobenzophenone in a step-growth SNAr polycondensation, building the alternating ether-ketone PEEK backbone.

SPO-PVDF-PEL.note: Vinylidene fluoride monomer (made from chlorodifluoromethane pyrolysis, itself from fluorspar/HF chemistry) is free-radically polymerized in suspension or emulsion to give PVDF.

POL-PVOH-PWD.reaction: Acetoxylation to VAM + free-radical polymerization + methanolysis
POL-PVOH-PWD.note: Ethylene and acetic acid combine (Wacker-type catalytic acetoxylation) to vinyl acetate monomer (VAM), which is free-radically polymerized to polyvinyl acetate; methanolysis (transesterification with methanol) then converts the acetate groups to hydroxyls, giving PVOH.

AGR-AN-GRN.note: Ammonia is oxidized (Ostwald process) to nitric acid, which is then neutralized with a second stream of ammonia in a simple acid-base reaction to form ammonium nitrate, granulated/prilled for handling.

AGR-DAP-GRN.note: Phosphate rock is acidulated with sulfuric acid (wet process) to phosphoric acid, which is then neutralized with ammonia to the diammonium salt, granulated to DAP fertilizer.

AGR-MOP-GRN.note: Mined sylvinite ore is physically (not chemically) processed — by froth flotation or hot-leach fractional crystallization — to separate potassium chloride from the co-mined sodium chloride, then compacted/granulated.

AGR-NH3-LIQ.reaction: Steam reforming to syngas + Haber-Bosch catalytic synthesis
AGR-NH3-LIQ.note: Methane is steam-reformed to hydrogen/syngas, combined with nitrogen from air, and catalytically synthesized to ammonia over an iron catalyst at high pressure and temperature (Haber-Bosch process).

AGR-UREA-GRN.note: Ammonia and CO2 (both available from the Haber-Bosch/reforming complex) react under pressure to ammonium carbamate, which is then thermally dehydrated to urea and prilled/granulated.

MIN-SOP-GRN.note: KCl and sulfuric acid react in a Mannheim rotary furnace at high temperature; hydrochloric acid gas is driven off and recovered, leaving potassium sulfate (SOP) as the solid product.

PFC-AOX-PWD.note: Phenol is alkylated with isobutylene under acid catalysis (Friedel-Crafts) to install bulky tert-butyl groups ortho/para to the hydroxyl, giving the sterically hindered phenol structure that confers antioxidant activity.

PFC-BPO-PWD.note: Benzoic acid is converted to benzoyl chloride, which then reacts with hydrogen peroxide (or sodium peroxide) under basic conditions to give the symmetrical diacyl peroxide, dibenzoyl peroxide.

PFC-DTBP-LIQ.note: Isobutylene reacts with hydrogen peroxide under acid catalysis to form tert-butyl hydroperoxide, which is then coupled with a second mole of isobutylene/acid to give the symmetrical di-tert-butyl peroxide.

PFC-H2O2-35.note: An alkylanthraquinone dissolved in an organic working solution is hydrogenated to the corresponding anthrahydroquinone, then re-oxidized with air, releasing hydrogen peroxide (extracted into water) and regenerating the anthraquinone for the next cycle.

PFC-H2O2-50.note: Same hydrogenation/air-oxidation anthraquinone cycle as the 35% grade, with the extracted peroxide solution concentrated further to reach 50% strength.

PFC-H2O2-EG.note: Same anthraquinone process as industrial-grade peroxide, followed by additional distillation/ion-exchange purification to remove trace metals and stabilizers for electronic (semiconductor wafer-cleaning) grade.

PFC-DINP-LIQ.note: Phthalic anhydride is esterified with two moles of isononanol under acid catalysis (water removed) to give diisononyl phthalate.

F21-AVOB-PWD.note: A tert-butylphenyl ketone (from Friedel-Crafts acylation) is condensed (Claisen condensation, base-catalyzed) with a p-methoxybenzoate ester to build the 1,3-diketone (dibenzoylmethane) structure of avobenzone.

OIL-DRA-LIQ.note: Alpha-olefins (from ethylene oligomerization) are polymerized under Ziegler-Natta or metallocene catalysis to ultra-high-molecular-weight poly(alpha-olefin), whose long chains reduce turbulent drag in pipeline flow.

F10-EHS-LIQ.note: Salicylic acid is esterified with 2-ethylhexanol under acid catalysis to give ethylhexyl salicylate.

F10-OCR-LIQ.note: Cyanoacetic acid is first esterified with 2-ethylhexanol, then the resulting ester's active methylene undergoes Knoevenagel condensation with benzophenone to build octocrylene's cyanoacrylate chromophore.

F10-OMC-LIQ.note: Anisaldehyde undergoes a Claisen-Schmidt (aldol) condensation to build the cinnamate double bond, and the resulting p-methoxycinnamic acid is esterified with 2-ethylhexanol to give octinoxate.

F10-HMS-LIQ.note: Salicylic acid is esterified with homomenthol (a terpene-type alcohol derived from isophorone/acetone chemistry) to give homosalate.

F10-EHT-PWD.note: Cyanuric chloride's three chlorines are sequentially displaced by the amino group of three equivalents of the 2-ethylhexyl ester of p-aminobenzoic acid, building the symmetric triazine-core UV filter ethylhexyl triazone.

PIG-FEO-BLK.note: Iron scrap is dissolved to a ferrous salt solution, then partially, controllably air-oxidized and precipitated so that ferrous and ferric iron co-precipitate in the 1:2 ratio of magnetite (Fe3O4), the black pigment.

PIG-FEO-RED.note: Iron scrap is dissolved in sulfuric acid to ferrous sulfate, then seeded and air-oxidized/calcined under controlled conditions (Penniman process) to grow hematite (Fe2O3) crystals, the red pigment.

PIG-FEO-YEL.note: Ferrous sulfate (from iron scrap and sulfuric acid) is seeded and slowly air-oxidized at controlled pH/temperature to precipitate goethite (FeOOH), the yellow iron oxide pigment.

PIG-PC-BLU.note: Phthalic anhydride (or phthalonitrile), urea, and a copper salt are heated together in a catalytic cyclotetramerization (Wyler process) to build the four-ring copper phthalocyanine macrocycle; some grades are further chlorinated to shift shade.

PIG-TIO2-CHL.note: Rutile ore is carbochlorinated (reacted with chlorine and coke at high temperature) to titanium tetrachloride (TiCl4), which is then oxidized with oxygen in the vapor phase to give pigment-grade TiO2 (chloride process).

PIG-TIO2-SUL.note: Ilmenite is digested with concentrated sulfuric acid to a titanyl sulfate/ferrous sulfate solution; the titanyl sulfate is hydrolyzed to hydrous titanium dioxide and calcined to give pigment-grade TiO2 (sulfate process).

feedstocks: Carbon black feedstock (heavy aromatic oil, CBFS)
PIG-CB-PEL.note: A heavy aromatic feedstock oil is injected into a natural-gas-fired furnace under sub-stoichiometric oxygen, thermally decomposing (incomplete combustion/pyrolysis) into fine carbon black particles, which are collected and pelletized.

PIG-ZNO-PWD.note: Metallic zinc is vaporized in a furnace and the vapor is burned in air (oxidized) to zinc oxide fume, which is collected as the fine white pigment/rubber-activator powder.

BCI-NA2CO3-PWD.note: Brine is saturated with ammonia and carbonated with CO2 (from calcined limestone) to precipitate sodium bicarbonate, which is then calcined to soda ash; alternatively, natural trona ore is simply mined and calcined directly.

BCI-NAOH-FLK.note: Brine is electrolyzed in a membrane cell to give caustic soda solution, chlorine, and hydrogen; the caustic solution is then evaporated and flaked/pearled to the 98% solid grade.

BCI-NAOH-SOL.note: Same brine electrolysis as flake caustic, with the resulting solution sold directly at 50% concentration rather than being further evaporated to a solid.

BCI-ALUM-GRN.note: Aluminium trihydrate (from bauxite refining, Bayer process) is digested with sulfuric acid, and the resulting aluminium sulfate solution is crystallized and dried to the granular anhydrous form.

BCI-ALUM-LIQ.note: Same aluminium trihydrate/sulfuric acid digestion as granular alum, with the product kept in solution (diluted to ~9% Al2O3) rather than crystallized.

BCI-PAC-10.note: Aluminium trihydrate is partially digested with hydrochloric acid (sub-stoichiometric versus full neutralization) so the aluminium hydrolyzes and polymerizes into the basic, partially-hydroxylated poly-aluminium-chloride species.

BCI-PAC-18.note: Same partial digestion chemistry as standard PAC, run at an even lower acid:alumina ratio to push the product to a higher basicity (18% Al2O3, more polymerized aluminium species).

BCI-FE2SO4-GRN.note: Iron is dissolved in sulfuric acid with oxidation (air or peroxide) to the ferric state, and the resulting ferric sulfate solution is evaporated/crystallized to the anhydrous granular product.

BCI-FE2SO4-LIQ.note: Same oxidative sulfuric-acid dissolution of iron as the granular grade, kept in solution and diluted to the 41% liquid product.

BCI-FECL3-ANH.note: Iron is dissolved in hydrochloric acid with oxidation (typically chlorine or air) to the ferric state, and the ferric chloride solution is evaporated/dried to the anhydrous solid.

BCI-FECL3-LIQ.note: Same oxidative HCl dissolution of iron as the anhydrous grade, sold in solution at 40% FeCl3 rather than dried.

BCI-FESO4-HEP.note: Iron is dissolved in sulfuric acid without deliberate oxidation (kept ferrous), and the ferrous sulfate solution is crystallized under conditions that retain seven waters of hydration (heptahydrate).

BCI-FESO4-MON.note: Same ferrous sulfate dissolution chemistry as the heptahydrate grade, with the crystals further dried/dehydrated to the monohydrate form.

BCI-HCL-EG.note: Chlorine and hydrogen are burned together (direct synthesis) to high-purity HCl gas, which is absorbed in water and further purified (distillation/ion exchange) to remove trace metals for electronic grade.

FOD-GLC-SYR.note: Corn starch is gelatinized and liquefied with alpha-amylase, then saccharified with glucoamylase to break the polysaccharide down into the dextrose/glucose syrup.

FOD-LACT-LIQ.note: Glucose is fermented by Lactobacillus bacteria (or engineered strains) to lactic acid, which is recovered and concentrated to the 80% food-grade solution.

BCI-H2SO4-LIQ.note: Sulfur is burned to SO2, catalytically oxidized to SO3 over vanadium pentoxide (contact process), and absorbed into existing sulfuric acid/water to give 98% sulfuric acid.

BCI-H3PO4-LIQ.note: Phosphate rock is acidulated with sulfuric acid, releasing phosphoric acid and precipitating gypsum (calcium sulfate) as a co-product, which is filtered off to leave the 85% phosphoric acid.

BCI-HCL-LIQ.note: Chlorine and hydrogen (both chlor-alkali co-products) are combusted together and the HCl gas absorbed in water to give the 33% commodity-grade hydrochloric acid.

CLN-NAOCL-LIQ.note: Chlorine gas is absorbed into cold caustic soda solution, disproportionating to sodium hypochlorite and sodium chloride, giving the 12-15% bleach solution.

F20-CA-LIG.note: Calcium bisulfite pulping of wood liberates lignin as calcium lignosulfonate in the spent sulfite liquor; this liquor is concentrated and spray-dried to the concrete-admixture product.

PAM-A-EMU.note: Acrylamide (made by catalytic or enzymatic hydration of acrylonitrile) is copolymerized with acrylic acid by a free-radical inverse (water-in-oil) emulsion process to build the anionic polyacrylamide (APAM), sold as a 45% W/O emulsion.

PAM-A-PWD.note: Same acrylamide/acrylic-acid free-radical copolymerization as the emulsion grade, run as a solution/gel polymerization and spray-dried to the 90% powder form.

PAM-A-SOL.note: Same acrylamide/acrylic-acid copolymerization, kept as an aqueous 30% solution rather than dried.

PAM-C-PWD.note: Acrylamide is copolymerized with DADMAC (itself made by quaternizing allyl chloride with dimethylamine) via free-radical polymerization to give cationic polyacrylamide (CPAM), spray-dried to powder.

PAM-C-SOL.note: Same acrylamide/DADMAC free-radical copolymerization as the CPAM powder, kept as a 30% aqueous solution.

PAM-N-PWD.note: Acrylamide alone is free-radically polymerized to non-ionic polyacrylamide (NPAM), then spray-dried to the 90% powder form.

PAM-N-SOL.note: Same acrylamide homopolymerization as the NPAM powder, kept as a 30% aqueous solution.

MIN-NACN-SOL.note: Ammonia and methane react catalytically with air (Andrussow process) to give hydrogen cyanide, which is then neutralized with caustic soda to form sodium cyanide.

MIN-NASIL-LIQ.note: Soda ash and sand are fused together in a furnace at high temperature to form a sodium silicate glass, which is then dissolved under pressure in water to give the liquid product.

MIN-CUSO4-PWD.note: Copper metal is oxidatively dissolved in sulfuric acid (air/oxygen as oxidant) to copper sulfate solution, which is crystallized to the pentahydrate.

MIN-GUAR-PWD.reaction: Mechanical dehusking, splitting, and milling (no chemical reaction)
MIN-GUAR-PWD.note: Guar seeds are mechanically dehusked and split to isolate the galactomannan-rich endosperm, which is ground/milled to the flotation-depressant powder — a physical processing step, not a chemical synthesis.

BCI-MEOH-LIQ.reaction: Steam reforming to syngas + catalytic methanol synthesis
BCI-MEOH-LIQ.note: Methane is steam-reformed to syngas (CO/H2), which is then catalytically synthesized (copper/zinc oxide/alumina catalyst, moderate pressure) to methanol.

BCI-MEG-LIQ.note: Ethylene is catalytically oxidized (silver catalyst) to ethylene oxide, which is then hydrolyzed (non-catalytic, excess water, high temperature) to monoethylene glycol.

BCI-FORM-LIQ.note: Methanol vapor is passed over a silver or metal-oxide catalyst with air, undergoing partial oxidation/dehydrogenation to formaldehyde, absorbed in water to give formalin.

BCI-CAOH2-PWD.note: Limestone is calcined (thermally decomposed, CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2) to quicklime, which is then slaked with water in an exothermic hydration reaction to give hydrated lime, Ca(OH)2.

FOD-STARCH-PWD.reaction: Wet milling (physical separation, no chemical reaction)
FOD-STARCH-PWD.note: Corn kernels are steeped, then mechanically milled and separated (hydrocyclones, screens) to isolate the starch fraction from protein, fiber, and germ — a physical separation process.

MIN-CACO3-GCC.note: Quarried limestone is simply crushed and finely ground (ball/roller milling) to the target particle size — a physical comminution process, not a synthesis.

MIN-CACO3-PCC.note: Limestone is calcined to lime, slaked with water to Ca(OH)2, then recarbonated with the CO2 recovered from the same calcination step to precipitate fine, controlled-morphology calcium carbonate (PCC).

ACT-CARB-MIN.note: Coal is pyrolyzed (carbonized) to a char, which is then activated with steam at high temperature to develop the internal micropore structure that gives activated carbon its adsorptive surface area.

ACT-CARB-COCO.note: Coconut shells are pyrolyzed to char and then steam-activated, the same two-step process as coal-based activated carbon, giving a harder, higher-surface-area product prized for liquid-phase applications.

MIN-BENT-PWD.note: Mined calcium-bentonite is treated with soda ash, exchanging calcium for sodium ions in the clay's interlayer (sodium activation) to boost swelling capacity, then thermally dried.

MIN-BARI-PWD.note: Mined barite ore is crushed and finely ground/milled to the target particle size for drilling-fluid/filler use — a physical processing step.

MIN-KAO-PWD.note: Mined kaolin is washed, classified, and ground to remove impurities and reach the target particle size distribution — physical beneficiation, not a chemical synthesis.

MIN-TALC-PWD.note: Mined talc ore is crushed and finely ground/micronized to the target particle size — a physical processing step.

MIN-FSIL-PWD.note: Silicon tetrachloride vapor is fed into a hydrogen/oxygen flame, where it hydrolyzes at high temperature to fine, high-surface-area fumed silica and HCl.

CLN-NACLO3-LIQ.note: Brine is electrolyzed in an undivided cell under conditions that favor further oxidation of the chlorine/hypochlorite intermediates through to chlorate, giving sodium chlorate directly.

CLN-PAA-LIQ.note: Acetic acid and hydrogen peroxide are combined with a strong-acid catalyst, establishing an equilibrium that forms peracetic acid (and water), which is used as the equilibrium mixture.

MIN-STPP-PWD.note: Phosphoric acid is neutralized with soda ash to a mono-/di-sodium phosphate mixture, which is then thermally condensed (water driven off at high temperature) to link the phosphate units into sodium tripolyphosphate.

POL-PDADMAC-LIQ.note: Allyl chloride is quaternized with dimethylamine to give the DADMAC monomer, which is then free-radically cyclopolymerized in water to build the polyDADMAC cationic polymer chain.

CLN-BAC-LIQ.note: A coconut-derived fatty dimethylamine reacts with benzyl chloride (from toluene's side-chain chlorination) in a quaternization reaction to give benzalkonium chloride.

MIN-NA2S-FLK.note: Sodium sulfate is reduced at high temperature by carbon (coal) in a carbothermic reduction reaction, releasing CO2/CO and leaving sodium sulfide, flaked for handling.

CLN-NAPERCARB-PWD.note: Soda ash reacts with concentrated hydrogen peroxide, and the resulting sodium carbonate-peroxide adduct is crystallized out as sodium percarbonate, a solid source of active oxygen.

feedstocks: Fatty acid chlorides (AKD route) or olefins (ASA route)
BCI-AKDASA-LIQ.note: For AKD, a fatty acyl chloride is dehydrohalogenated to a ketene and dimerized to the beta-lactone alkyl ketene dimer; for ASA, an internal olefin instead undergoes an Alder-ene reaction directly with maleic anhydride to give the alkenyl succinic anhydride.

BCI-NAGLUC-PWD.note: Dextrose is oxidized (fermentation with Aspergillus niger and its glucose oxidase enzyme, or catalytically) to gluconic acid, which is neutralized with caustic soda to sodium gluconate.

BCI-H2SO4-ELEC.note: Same sulfur-burning/SO3-absorption contact process as industrial sulfuric acid, followed by additional distillation/purification to reach electronic-grade trace-metal specifications.

BCI-NH3-ELEC.note: Same steam-reforming/Haber-Bosch ammonia synthesis as agricultural ammonia, with additional distillation/purification to reach electronic-grade purity for semiconductor use.

BCI-NABROM-LIQ.note: Bromine, recovered from natural brine by oxidizing bromide with chlorine, is reacted with sodium carbonate/caustic soda in a reduction-neutralization step to give sodium bromide brine.

BCI-ZNBROM-LIQ.note: Zinc oxide or metal is neutralized/dissolved with hydrobromic acid (itself derived from bromine chemistry) to give the dense zinc bromide brine used in oilfield completion fluids.

BCI-NAMBS-PWD.note: Sulfur dioxide gas is absorbed into a soda ash solution, forming sodium metabisulfite, which is then crystallized and dried.

BCI-KMNO4-PWD.note: Manganese ore is fused with potassium hydroxide and oxidized by air to potassium manganate, which is then electrolytically oxidized further to potassium permanganate.

CLN-CAHYPO-PWD.note: Chlorine gas reacts with slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) in a chlorination/disproportionation reaction to give calcium hypochlorite, the solid bleaching/sanitizing powder.

MIN-MSTARCH-PWD.reaction: Chemical modification (oxidation, esterification, or etherification, grade-dependent)
MIN-MSTARCH-PWD.note: Native corn starch is chemically modified — commonly by oxidation (sodium hypochlorite) or esterification/etherification, depending on the target functional grade — to alter its viscosity, stability, or gelling behavior for food use.

BCI-LIOH-PWD.note: Spodumene ore is roasted to convert it to the reactive beta form, leached with sulfuric acid to lithium sulfate solution, then causticized with lime/soda ash to precipitate lithium hydroxide.

BCI-ZNSO4-PWD.note: Zinc metal, oxide, or ore is leached/dissolved in sulfuric acid, and the resulting zinc sulfate solution is crystallized to the powder product.

BCI-MNSO4-PWD.note: Manganese ore is reductively leached with sulfuric acid (often with a reducing agent to convert Mn(IV) to soluble Mn(II)), and the manganese sulfate solution is crystallized to powder.

MIN-PSIL-PWD.note: Sodium silicate solution is precipitated with sulfuric acid under controlled pH/temperature to build the fine, highly dispersible silica particle structure needed for tire-grade precipitated silica.

MIN-XANTH-GRN.note: An alcohol (isopropanol or amyl alcohol) reacts with carbon disulfide in the presence of caustic soda/potash, the alkoxide adding across CS2 to form the xanthate salt used as a flotation collector.

BCI-HF-LIQ.note: Fluorspar reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid in a rotary kiln at high temperature (double-displacement reaction), releasing hydrogen fluoride gas, which is condensed/absorbed to anhydrous or aqueous HF.

MIN-NDPR-OXD.note: The mixed rare-earth concentrate is leached with acid, then the individual rare earths are separated by a long liquid-liquid solvent-extraction cascade; the isolated neodymium/praseodymium fraction is precipitated and calcined to the magnet-grade oxide.

BCI-BENZ-LIQ.note: Naphtha is catalytically reformed (platforming) to a BTX-rich reformate, from which benzene is separated by solvent extraction and fractional distillation, the same route used for toluene and xylenes.

BCI-EO-LIQ.note: Ethylene is directly oxidized with oxygen over a silver catalyst (partial oxidation, avoiding full combustion to CO2) to give ethylene oxide.

BCI-ACN-LIQ.note: Propylene, ammonia, and air react together over a bismuth-molybdate catalyst (Sohio ammoxidation process) to give acrylonitrile directly in a single catalytic step.

BCI-AA-LIQ.note: Propylene is catalytically oxidized in two stages — first to acrolein, then further oxidized to acrylic acid — over selective metal-oxide catalysts.

BCI-PHOL-SOL.note: Benzene is alkylated with propylene to cumene, air-oxidized to cumene hydroperoxide, and acid-cleaved (Hock rearrangement) to give phenol and acetone as co-products.

BCI-BPA-PWD.note: Phenol and acetone condense under acid catalysis (typically with a thiol promoter), two phenol molecules bridging across the acetone carbonyl to form bisphenol A.

BCI-CHEX-LIQ.note: Benzene is catalytically hydrogenated (nickel or platinum catalyst, high pressure) to fully saturate the aromatic ring, giving cyclohexane.

BCI-PX-LIQ.note: Naphtha is catalytically reformed to mixed xylenes, from which the para isomer is isolated by selective adsorption (UOP Parex process) or low-temperature crystallization.

BCI-OX-LIQ.note: Same catalytic reforming as paraxylene; the ortho isomer, having the highest boiling point of the three xylene isomers, is separated by straightforward fractional distillation.

BCI-PTA-PWD.note: Paraxylene is oxidized with air in acetic acid solvent over a cobalt/manganese/bromide catalyst (Amoco MC process), oxidizing both methyl groups to carboxylic acids to give purified terephthalic acid.

BCI-PIA-PWD.note: Meta-xylene is oxidized by the same cobalt/manganese/bromide-catalyzed acetic-acid-solvent process used for PTA, giving purified isophthalic acid.

BCI-PO-LIQ.note: Propylene reacts with hypochlorous acid (generated in situ from chlorine and water) to form propylene chlorohydrin, which is then dehydrohalogenated with lime to close the epoxide ring and give propylene oxide.

BCI-MMA-LIQ.note: Acetone reacts with hydrogen cyanide to acetone cyanohydrin, which is treated with sulfuric acid and methanol in a Ritter-type rearrangement/esterification to give methyl methacrylate directly.

BCI-NPG-PWD.note: Formaldehyde and isobutyraldehyde undergo base-catalyzed aldol condensation, and the resulting hydroxypivaldehyde is reduced (catalytic hydrogenation or Cannizzaro) to neopentyl glycol.

BCI-TMP-PWD.note: n-Butyraldehyde undergoes a triple aldol condensation with formaldehyde, and the excess formaldehyde is consumed in a Cannizzaro reaction (with NaOH) that simultaneously reduces the aldol adduct to trimethylolpropane.

BCI-PENTA-PWD.note: Acetaldehyde undergoes a fourfold aldol condensation with formaldehyde (calcium hydroxide catalyst), and a final Cannizzaro reaction with excess formaldehyde reduces the tetra-aldol to pentaerythritol.

BCI-HEX1-LIQ.note: Ethylene is selectively trimerized over a chromium-based homogeneous catalyst to give 1-hexene directly (rather than the broader oligomer distribution of SHOP-type processes).

BCI-MEA-LIQ.note: Ethylene oxide reacts with aqueous ammonia in a ring-opening addition; the ratio of reactants controls the mono-, di-, and tri-ethanolamine product distribution.

BCI-POLYOL-LIQ.note: Propylene oxide (and, for some grades, ethylene oxide) is polymerized onto a glycerine (or other polyol) initiator under base catalysis, the ring-opening addition building the polyether polyol chain to the target hydroxyl number.

BCI-LAO8-LIQ.note: Ethylene is oligomerized over a nickel-phosphine catalyst (Shell Higher Olefin Process) and the resulting alpha-olefin distribution is fractionated to isolate the C8 (1-octene) cut.

BCI-LAO1012-LIQ.note: Same SHOP ethylene oligomerization as 1-octene, with fractional distillation isolating the C10-C12 (1-decene/1-dodecene) cut.

BCI-LAO1418-LIQ.note: Same SHOP ethylene oligomerization, with the heavier C14-C18 detergent-range alpha-olefin cut isolated by distillation.

BCI-NEOFLO-LIQ.note: SHOP-derived linear alpha olefins are subjected to an isomerization/disproportionation catalytic loop that migrates and redistributes the double bond position, converting terminal alpha olefins into the internal-olefin structure used in EOR/drilling-fluid applications.

BCI-STY-LIQ.note: Benzene is alkylated with ethylene (Friedel-Crafts) to ethylbenzene, which is then catalytically dehydrogenated (iron-oxide catalyst, steam) to styrene; an alternative SMPO route co-produces styrene with propylene oxide.

BCI-BD-LIQ.reaction: Extractive distillation (separation, not a chemical reaction)
BCI-BD-LIQ.note: Butadiene is not synthesized directly but recovered as a co-product of naphtha steam cracking (ethylene production); it is isolated from the mixed C4 raffinate stream by extractive distillation using a selective solvent (e.g. NMP or DMF).

BCI-DEG-LIQ.note: When ethylene oxide is hydrolyzed to monoethylene glycol, some EO reacts with the MEG already formed rather than water, giving the dimeric diethylene glycol as a co-product, separated by distillation.

BCI-TEG-LIQ.note: Further EO addition onto diethylene glycol gives the trimeric triethylene glycol, recovered from the same EO-hydrolysis product mix by distillation.

BCI-EC-LIQ.note: Ethylene oxide reacts with CO2 under catalysis in a cycloaddition reaction, inserting the CO2 into the epoxide ring to build the five-membered cyclic carbonate, ethylene carbonate.

BCI-PC-LIQ.note: Propylene oxide reacts with CO2 in the same catalytic cycloaddition used for ethylene carbonate, giving propylene carbonate.

MIN-EMULEXP-LIQ.reaction: Water-in-oil emulsification (physical process, not a chemical synthesis)
MIN-EMULEXP-LIQ.note: A hot concentrated ammonium nitrate solution is dispersed as fine droplets within a continuous fuel-oil/wax phase, stabilized by an emulsifier, to give the water-in-oil emulsion — a physical formulation step rather than a chemical reaction.

BCI-ACETAC-LIQ.note: Methanol is carbonylated with carbon monoxide over a rhodium (Monsanto) or iridium (Cativa) catalyst system to give acetic acid directly.

BCI-VAM-LIQ.note: Ethylene, acetic acid, and oxygen react over a palladium catalyst in a Wacker-type acetoxylation to give vinyl acetate monomer.

BCI-CAPRO-PWD.reaction: Oxidation to cyclohexanone + oximation + Beckmann rearrangement
BCI-CAPRO-PWD.note: Cyclohexane is oxidized to a cyclohexanol/cyclohexanone mix, converted to the oxime with hydroxylamine, and then subjected to the acid-catalyzed Beckmann rearrangement (with oleum) to insert nitrogen into the ring, giving caprolactam plus an ammonium sulfate co-product.

BCI-ADIPAC-PWD.reaction: Air oxidation to KA oil + nitric acid oxidation
BCI-ADIPAC-PWD.note: Cyclohexane is air-oxidized to a cyclohexanol/cyclohexanone mixture (KA oil), which is then further oxidized with nitric acid, cleaving the ring to give the linear diacid, adipic acid.

BCI-PHAN-PWD.note: Orthoxylene is oxidized in the vapor phase over a vanadium pentoxide catalyst, both methyl groups being oxidized and the ring closing to give phthalic anhydride.

BCI-MALAN-PWD.note: n-Butane is oxidized in the vapor phase over a vanadium-phosphorus-oxide catalyst, losing four hydrogens and gaining three oxygens in a single catalytic step to give maleic anhydride.

BCI-ANIL-LIQ.note: Benzene is nitrated with nitric acid to nitrobenzene, which is then catalytically hydrogenated to reduce the nitro group to an amine, giving aniline.

BCI-ACAN-LIQ.note: Acetic acid is thermally cracked (pyrolyzed) to ketene, which is then reacted with a second mole of acetic acid to give acetic anhydride.

BCI-MELAM-PWD.note: Urea is heated under pressure with a catalyst, decomposing and condensing (releasing ammonia and CO2) to build the triazine ring structure of melamine.

BCI-ECH-LIQ.reaction: Allylic chlorination + hypochlorous acid addition + dehydrohalogenation
BCI-ECH-LIQ.note: Propylene is allylically chlorinated to allyl chloride, which reacts with hypochlorous acid to a dichlorohydrin; treatment with a base (lime/NaOH) then dehydrohalogenates the intermediate, closing the epoxide ring to give epichlorohydrin.

feedstocks: Maleic anhydride (as maleic acid in water)
BCI-FUMAC-PWD.note: Maleic anhydride is hydrolyzed to maleic acid (the cis isomer) and then catalytically isomerized (heat/catalyst) to its more stable trans isomer, fumaric acid.

BCI-GLUAC-LIQ.note: Glucose is oxidized by Aspergillus niger fermentation (via its glucose oxidase enzyme) to gluconic acid, recovered as the aqueous solution.

BCI-HNO3-LIQ.note: Ammonia is catalytically oxidized over a platinum-rhodium gauze to nitric oxide, which is further oxidized to NO2 and absorbed in water (Ostwald process) to give nitric acid.

ADV-ARAM-FIB.note: Terephthaloyl chloride (from PTA activated with phosgene/thionyl chloride) reacts with para-phenylenediamine in a low-temperature solution polycondensation to build the rigid-rod aramid polymer, which is then dry-jet wet spun into fibre.

ADV-CF-TOW.note: Acrylonitrile is free-radically polymerized to polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and spun into precursor fibre, which is oxidatively stabilized in air (~200-300°C) and then carbonized at high temperature (1000-1500°C) under inert atmosphere, driving off non-carbon atoms to leave the graphitic carbon fibre structure.

ADV-EGLASS-CSM.note: Continuous E-glass roving is mechanically chopped into short strands and randomly bonded with a resin binder into a mat — a physical converting step, not a chemical synthesis.

ADV-EGLASS-ROV.note: Silica sand, limestone, and alumina-bearing minerals are melted together in a furnace at very high temperature, then drawn through platinum bushings into continuous glass filaments (fiberization) and wound onto spools as roving — a melt-and-draw thermal process rather than a discrete chemical reaction.

FLU-VII-OCP.note: Ethylene and propylene are copolymerized under Ziegler-Natta catalysis to a low-crystallinity, oil-soluble ethylene-propylene copolymer used as a viscosity index improver.

FLU-VII-PMA.note: MMA is free-radically polymerized in a lubricant base-oil solvent to give the polymethacrylate viscosity index improver directly as an oil solution.

FLU-ZDDP-LIQ.note: 2-Ethylhexanol reacts with phosphorus pentasulfide to form a dialkyl dithiophosphoric acid, which is then neutralized with zinc oxide to give the antiwear additive ZDDP.

FLU-BO1-SN150.note: A vacuum-distilled crude oil cut is solvent-extracted (removing aromatics/polar compounds) and solvent-dewaxed, giving the conventionally-refined Group I base oil.

FLU-BO2-150N.note: A vacuum-distilled crude cut is hydroprocessed (catalytic hydrocracking and hydrofinishing under hydrogen) rather than solvent-refined, giving the higher-purity, higher-VI Group II base oil.

FLU-BO3-4CST.note: A vacuum-distilled crude cut is severely hydrocracked and catalytically hydroisomerized (waxy paraffins converted to branched isoparaffins) to give the high-VI Group III base oil.

FLU-PAO-4.note: Linear alpha-olefins (typically 1-decene) are cationically oligomerized (BF3 catalyst) and the resulting olefinic oligomer is hydrogenated to the saturated, low-viscosity polyalphaolefin (PAO 4).

FLU-PAO-68.note: Same LAO cationic oligomerization/hydrogenation route as PAO 4, run to a higher degree of oligomerization to reach the medium-viscosity PAO 6/8 grade.

LUB-PAG-LIQ.note: Propylene oxide and ethylene oxide are copolymerized onto an alcohol initiator under base catalysis (ring-opening addition), building the polyalkylene glycol lubricant base stock.

LUB-ESTER-LIQ.note: Oleic or stearic fatty acids are esterified with a polyol (trimethylolpropane or pentaerythritol) under acid catalysis, water removed, to give the synthetic ester base stock.

SIL-EMU-35.note: Finished PDMS fluid is mechanically dispersed into fine droplets in water, stabilized by a fatty-alcohol-ethoxylate emulsifier — a physical formulation step, not a further chemical synthesis of the silicone itself.

SIL-EMU-60.note: Same mechanical emulsification of finished PDMS as the 35% grade, formulated to a higher (60%) active-silicone concentration for industrial use.

SIL-PDMS-HGH.note: Silicon metal reacts with methyl chloride over a copper catalyst (Rochow-Müller direct process) to give methylchlorosilanes, which are hydrolyzed and then acid/base-equilibrated (condensation/redistribution) to build PDMS chains to a high degree of polymerization (>10,000 cSt).

SIL-PDMS-LOW.note: Same direct-process/hydrolysis route as high-viscosity PDMS, equilibrated to a shorter average chain length to give the low-viscosity (50-1000 cSt) fluid.

SIL-RTV1-LIQ.note: Silanol-terminated PDMS is compounded with an acetoxysilane crosslinker and fumed silica filler; on exposure to atmospheric moisture after application, the acetoxy groups hydrolyze and condense with the silanol, curing the one-part sealant (releasing acetic acid).

SIL-RTV2-LIQ.reaction: Two-part addition (hydrosilylation) or condensation cure (on mixing)
SIL-RTV2-LIQ.note: A vinyl- (or silanol-) functional PDMS base is supplied separately from a crosslinker/catalyst part; mixing the two triggers a platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation (or tin-catalyzed condensation) cure into the crosslinked silicone.

SIL-SURF-LIQ.note: A hydride-functional PDMS backbone is grafted with an allyl-terminated polyether via platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation, giving the amphiphilic silicone-polyether surfactant.

F16-TPP-LIQ.note: Phosphorus oxychloride reacts with three equivalents of phenol (base present to absorb the HCl released) in a Schotten-Baumann-type esterification to give triphenyl phosphate.

F16-ATMP-LIQ.note: Ammonia, formaldehyde, and phosphorous acid react together in a Mannich-type (Moedritzer-Irani) condensation, installing three aminomethylenephosphonic acid arms on the nitrogen to build ATMP.

F16-HEDP-LIQ.note: Phosphorus trichloride reacts directly with acetic acid, followed by hydrolysis, to build the geminal bis-phosphonate carbon center that gives HEDP its strong metal-chelating and scale-inhibiting activity.

F19-THPS-SOL.note: Phosphine reacts with four equivalents of formaldehyde (acid-catalyzed Mannich-type addition) to build tetrakis(hydroxymethyl)phosphonium chloride (THPC), which is then converted with sulfuric acid to the sulfate salt, THPS.

MIN-AEROPHINE-LIQ.note: A dialkylphosphine reacts with elemental sulfur to form a dithiophosphinic acid, which is neutralized with caustic soda to give the sodium dithiophosphinate flotation collector.

F16-DTPMP-LIQ.note: Diethylenetriamine's five N-H sites are all reacted with formaldehyde and phosphorous acid in a Moedritzer-Irani (Mannich-type) condensation, installing five phosphonomethyl arms to build DTPMP.

F16-PBTC-LIQ.note: Phosphorous acid (or phosphorus trichloride) adds across the maleic anhydride double bond in a phospha-Michael-type addition, and subsequent hydrolysis/ring-opening gives the phosphonate-tricarboxylate structure of PBTC.

F18-SAP-AGR.note: Acrylic acid is partially neutralized with caustic soda, then free-radically polymerized in aqueous solution with a small amount of a difunctional crosslinker, building the lightly crosslinked sodium polyacrylate network that swells to absorb water.

F18-SAP-HYG.note: Same partial-neutralization/free-radical crosslinking polymerization as agricultural-grade SAP, tuned to a finer crosslink density and particle size for hygiene-product absorbency performance, then dried and ground.

F22-LAR-EU.note: Air is compressed, cooled, and liquefied, then fractionally distilled in a cryogenic column to separate argon (which co-elutes near oxygen) from nitrogen and oxygen — a physical separation, not a chemical reaction.

F22-LIN-EU.note: Same cryogenic air-separation distillation as argon and oxygen; nitrogen, the lowest-boiling major component, is taken off the top of the column.

F22-LOX-EU.note: Same cryogenic air-separation distillation; oxygen, the highest-boiling major component, is recovered from the bottom of the column.

F22-R1234YF-EU.note: Hydrofluoric acid (from fluorspar) is used to fluorinate a chlorinated three-carbon building block through a proprietary, patent-protected catalytic fluorination sequence developed jointly by Honeywell and Chemours to build the unsaturated HFO-1234yf molecule.

F22-R134A-EU.note: Trichloroethylene is catalytically hydrofluorinated (antimony or chromium catalyst) with HF, substituting chlorine atoms for fluorine, to give HFC-134a.

F22-R32-EU.note: Methylene chloride (from methanol/methane chlorination) is catalytically hydrofluorinated with HF, replacing chlorine with fluorine, to give difluoromethane (HFC-32).

F22-R410A-EU.reaction: Physical blending (near-azeotropic mixture, not a reaction)
F22-R410A-EU.note: R-32 and R-125 (each separately synthesized by HF fluorination of a chlorocarbon precursor) are physically blended in a fixed ratio to form the near-azeotropic R-410A refrigerant mixture.

feedstocks: Natural gas (via steam reforming/ammonia process off-gas)
F22-CO2-EU.note: CO2-rich off-gas from natural-gas steam reforming (e.g. ammonia synthesis) is scrubbed with a hot potassium carbonate (Benfield) amine solution, which selectively absorbs and then releases the CO2 on regeneration, giving purified, liquefiable CO2 — a physical/chemical absorption-desorption cycle rather than a synthesis.

F22-H2-EU.note: Methane reacts catalytically with steam at high temperature (steam methane reforming) to give a syngas mixture, from which hydrogen is purified (e.g. pressure-swing adsorption) as the dominant product.

F23-LYS-EU.note: Glucose is fermented by an engineered Corynebacterium glutamicum strain (using ammonia as the nitrogen source) to L-lysine, which is recovered and crystallized as the hydrochloride salt.

F23-MET-EU.note: Acrolein and methanethiol undergo a thia-Michael addition to give methylthiopropionaldehyde (MMP), which then reacts with HCN and ammonia in a Strecker-type/Bucherer-Bergs hydantoin synthesis; base hydrolysis of the hydantoin ring releases DL-methionine.

F23-THR-EU.note: Glucose is fermented by an engineered bacterial strain (typically E. coli or Corynebacterium) to L-threonine, recovered and dried to the feed-grade powder.

F23-VITD3-EU.note: Cholesterol is dehydrogenated to 7-dehydrocholesterol, which is then photochemically ring-opened by UV light to previtamin D3 and thermally isomerized to cholecalciferol (vitamin D3).

F23-VITE-EU.note: Isophytol condenses with trimethylhydroquinone under acid catalysis (Friedel-Crafts-type alkylation and ring cyclization) to build the tocopherol chromanol ring, which is then acetylated to the stable tocopheryl acetate form.

F23-NIAC-FG-EU.note: 3-Cyanopyridine is partially hydrolyzed (catalytic, controlled to stop at the amide rather than the full carboxylic acid) to give niacinamide directly.

F21-ASCOR-PWD.note: Glucose is catalytically hydrogenated to sorbitol, microbially fermented (Acetobacter) to L-sorbose, then taken through acetonation, catalytic oxidation, and acid-catalyzed lactonization/enolization (the classical Reichstein sequence) to ascorbic acid.

F21-NIAC-PWD.note: 3-Cyanopyridine (from catalytic ammoxidation of 3-picoline) undergoes controlled ammonolysis/partial hydrolysis of the nitrile to the amide, giving cosmetic-grade niacinamide.

BIO-GELA-PWD.note: Bovine hide collagen is pretreated with lime (alkaline process) or acid to loosen the fibre structure, then extracted by controlled hot-water hydrolysis, which partially breaks down the collagen triple helix into soluble gelatin.

BIO-PECT-PWD.note: Citrus peel is extracted with hot dilute acid, which solubilizes the pectin from the plant cell walls; the extract is then precipitated with alcohol (or a metal salt) and dried to powder.

BIO-CARR-PWD.note: Red seaweed is extracted with hot alkali (KOH/NaOH), which solubilizes the sulfated galactan carrageenan; the extract is then precipitated with potassium chloride (or isopropanol) and dried.

BIO-NAALG-PWD.reaction: Alkaline extraction + acid/calcium precipitation + sodium conversion
BIO-NAALG-PWD.note: Brown seaweed is extracted with sodium carbonate (soda ash), solubilizing alginic acid as its sodium salt; the alginate is precipitated (as calcium alginate or alginic acid), then converted back to the soluble sodium salt and dried.

F23-CHCL-PWD.note: Ethylene oxide reacts with trimethylamine in a ring-opening addition to give choline (as the hydroxide/base), which is then neutralized with hydrochloric acid to give choline chloride.

F23-DPAN-LIQ.note: Isobutyraldehyde and formaldehyde undergo an aldol condensation building pantolactone, which is then condensed (amidated) with beta-alanine (itself from acrylonitrile hydration/hydrogenation) to give D-panthenol.

F23-BCAR-PWD.note: C15 terpene aldehyde/phosphonium-salt fragments (built from propylene-derived isoprenoid intermediates) are coupled via a Wittig olefination, using a triphenylphosphine-derived ylide, to assemble the full C40 beta-carotene backbone.

F23-ASTA-PWD.note: Citral-derived carotenoid fragments are coupled via Wittig olefination (triphenylphosphine ylide chemistry, as with beta-carotene) to build the C40 backbone, which is then oxidized to install the keto/hydroxyl groups that distinguish astaxanthin from beta-carotene.

F23-HYD3-PWD.note: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is selectively hydroxylated at the 25-position (chemical or enzymatic/microbial hydroxylation), replicating the first step of the body's own vitamin D activation and bypassing hepatic conversion.

F23-VITK3-PWD.note: 2-Methylnaphthalene is catalytically oxidized to menadione (vitamin K3), which is then complexed with sodium metabisulfite to give the stable, water-dispersible MSB salt form.

F23-VITB6-PWD.note: Acrylonitrile, acetaldehyde, and formaldehyde are built up through a multi-step oxazole-intermediate cyclization sequence to construct the substituted pyridine ring of pyridoxine, which is then converted to its hydrochloride salt.

F23-SALAC-PWD.note: Phenol is first converted to sodium phenolate with caustic soda, which then reacts with CO2 under heat and pressure (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction) to carboxylate the ring; acidification with sulfuric acid liberates salicylic acid.

F23-GLYAC-LIQ.reaction: Acid-catalyzed carbonylation (Reppe-type) or chloroacetic acid hydrolysis
F23-GLYAC-LIQ.note: Formaldehyde, carbon monoxide, and water react under strong acid catalysis (Reppe-type carbonylation) to give glycolic acid directly; an alternative commercial route instead hydrolyzes chloroacetic acid with caustic soda to the same product.

FOD-SORB-LIQ.note: Glucose is catalytically hydrogenated (nickel catalyst, high pressure) — the aldehyde group reduced to a hydroxyl — to give sorbitol.

FOD-MALTO-PWD.note: Corn or potato starch is partially hydrolyzed (enzymatic or mild acid hydrolysis, stopped well short of complete conversion to glucose) to give the shorter-chain, low-sweetness maltodextrin.

F24-HEUR-EU.note: MDI's isocyanate groups react with PEG's terminal hydroxyls in a step-growth urethane-forming polymerization, building a water-soluble PEG backbone capped at each end with a hydrophobic group, giving the associative (HEUR) thickener.

F24-GHPTC-PWD.note: Natural guar gum's hydroxyl groups are etherified (Williamson-type reaction, base-catalyzed) with the quaternary epoxide reagent glycidyltrimethylammonium chloride, installing the cationic hydroxypropyltrimonium group.

F24-XG-EU.note: Glucose is fermented by the bacterium Xanthomonas campestris, which excretes the branched polysaccharide xanthan gum as a protective biofilm; the gum is recovered by alcohol precipitation and dried.

F24-HEC-EU.note: Cellulose is alkalized with NaOH to activate its hydroxyls, then etherified with ethylene oxide (ring-opening Williamson-type addition) to install hydroxyethyl side groups, giving hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC).

F24-CARB-EU.note: Acrylic acid is free-radically polymerized with a small amount of a divinyl (allyl ether-type) crosslinker in solution, building the lightly crosslinked, high-molecular-weight polyacrylic acid network of carbomer 940.

F24-PQ10-PWD.note: HEC's residual hydroxyls are further etherified with the quaternary epoxide reagent glycidyltrimethylammonium chloride (itself built from epichlorohydrin and trimethylamine), giving the cationic cellulose derivative polyquaternium-10.

F25-EDTA-EU.note: Ethylenediamine's four N-H groups react with formaldehyde and hydrogen cyanide in a Strecker-type cyanomethylation, and base hydrolysis of the resulting nitrile groups gives the four carboxylate arms of EDTA, isolated as its tetrasodium salt.

F25-GLDA-EU.note: L-Glutamic acid's free amine adds across acrylonitrile in a Michael-type cyanoethylation, and base hydrolysis of the resulting nitrile groups gives the diacetic-acid arms that make GLDA a biodegradable chelating agent.

F25-MGDA-EU.note: A primary amine (glycine-derived) undergoes Michael-type cyanoethylation with acrylonitrile, and base hydrolysis of the nitrile groups gives the diacetic-acid arms of methylglycinediacetic acid (MGDA).

CLN-CA-PWD.note: Corn-derived glucose is fermented by Aspergillus niger, which secretes citric acid; the acid is recovered (typically by calcium salt precipitation and re-acidification) and dried to anhydrous powder.

FOD-CA-ANH.note: Same Aspergillus niger glucose fermentation as cleaning-grade citric acid, purified and crystallized to food-grade specification.

F26-GLUT-EU.note: 1,5-Pentanediol (built up from propylene-derived intermediates) is catalytically oxidized/dehydrogenated at both terminal hydroxyls to give the dialdehyde glutaraldehyde.

F26-PHEOH-EU.note: Phenol's phenolate anion opens the ethylene oxide ring in a base-catalyzed Williamson-type etherification, giving phenoxyethanol.

F26-BIT-EU.note: Thiodiglycol (from ethylene oxide and hydrogen sulfide) is chlorinated and cyclized (ring closure onto an aniline-derived nitrogen) to build the benzisothiazolinone (BIT) ring system.

F26-MIT-EU.note: Dichlorobutene reacts with methylamine in a cyclization that closes the five-membered isothiazolinone ring, giving methylisothiazolinone (MIT).

PRES-NABENZ-PWD.note: Toluene's methyl group is catalytically oxidized (air, cobalt/manganese catalyst) to benzoic acid, which is then neutralized with caustic soda to give sodium benzoate.

PRES-KSRB-PWD.note: Ethylene-derived acetaldehyde is aldol-condensed to crotonaldehyde, which is further condensed (with ketene or malonic acid) to sorbic acid; neutralization with potassium hydroxide gives potassium sorbate.

F27-PEA-EU.note: Benzene is alkylated with ethylene oxide under Lewis-acid (AlCl3) Friedel-Crafts catalysis, the epoxide ring opening onto the aromatic ring to give 2-phenylethanol (phenylethyl alcohol) directly.

F27-GAL-SOL.note: Galaxolide (HHCB) is built through a multi-step, industry-proprietary sequence of Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation reactions on substituted indane/tetrahydronaphthalene-type aromatics; the exact process route is not publicly disclosed by producers.

F27-BION-EU.reaction: Ethynylation + isomerization + aldol condensation + acid-catalyzed cyclization
F27-BION-EU.note: Acetone is ethynylated with acetylene to a C5 alcohol, which is isomerized and aldol-condensed with a second acetone equivalent to pseudoionone; acid-catalyzed cyclization of pseudoionone then closes the six-membered ring to give beta-ionone.

F27-CIT-EU.note: Pinene is acid-catalyzed isomerized to myrcene and taken through further addition/hydrogenation steps (via citronellal) to give the terpene alcohol citronellol.

feedstocks: Ho wood oil / rosewood oil (natural extract)
F27-LIN-EU.reaction: Steam distillation (natural extraction, not a chemical synthesis)
F27-LIN-EU.note: Natural linalool is not synthesized but isolated by steam distillation of ho wood oil or rosewood oil, followed by fractional distillation to purify the linalool-rich fraction.

F27-DLIM-LIQ.reaction: Steam distillation/cold pressing (natural extraction, not a chemical synthesis)
F27-DLIM-LIQ.note: d-Limonene is recovered from citrus peel (a byproduct of juice processing) by steam distillation or cold-pressing rather than being chemically synthesized, then purified by distillation.

F27-CTRL-LIQ.note: Isobutylene and formaldehyde are built up through a multi-step condensation sequence (Prins-type reactions extending the isoprenoid carbon chain) to construct citral, an important terpenoid and vitamin-A synthesis intermediate.

F28-AZOX-CN.reaction: Multi-step etherification, oxime formation, and ester condensation
F28-AZOX-CN.note: Salicylonitrile is elaborated through several steps — aryl ether formation with a chlorophenol partner, oxime formation, and condensation with methyl (E)-3-methoxyacrylate — to build the strobilurin fungicide azoxystrobin.

F28-MANZ-CN.reaction: Dithiocarbamate formation + metal coordination complex formation
F28-MANZ-CN.note: Ethylenediamine reacts with carbon disulfide to form the bis-dithiocarbamate ligand, which then coordinates with manganese and zinc ions to form the mixed-metal ethylenebisdithiocarbamate (EBDC) complex, mancozeb.

F28-PROP-CN.note: Epichlorohydrin is etherified with 2,4-dichlorophenol, and the resulting chloromethyl group is then displaced by 1,2,4-triazole in a nucleophilic substitution to build the triazole fungicide propiconazole.

F28-CHLOR-CN.note: Phosphorus trichloride is converted to a thiophosphoryl chloride intermediate, which is esterified with 3,5,6-trichloro-2-pyridinol (built via chlorination of a pyridine intermediate) to give the organophosphate insecticide chlorpyrifos.

F28-CYPR-CN.note: meta-Phenoxybenzaldehyde reacts with hydrogen cyanide to form a cyanohydrin, which is then esterified with cyclopropanecarboxylic acid (in its acid-chloride form) to give the pyrethroid insecticide cypermethrin.

F28-IMID-CN.note: 2-Chloro-5-chloromethylpyridine's chloromethyl group displaces a proton on a nitromethane-derived nitroimidazolidine ring nitrogen in a nucleophilic substitution/condensation, giving the neonicotinoid insecticide imidacloprid.

AGR-GLYP-TC.note: Glycine's amine reacts with formaldehyde and phosphorous acid in a Mannich-type phosphonomethylation, installing the phosphonomethyl group that gives glyphosate its herbicidal activity.

AGR-24D-LIQ.note: Phenol is chlorinated to 2,4-dichlorophenol, whose phenolate then displaces the chlorine of chloroacetic acid in a Williamson-type etherification to give the herbicide 2,4-D.

AGR-LCHT-TC.note: A chlorinated DMPB-acid intermediate is esterified with a cyanohydrin ester built from meta-phenoxybenzaldehyde and hydrogen cyanide — the same general esterification chemistry family used for cypermethrin — to give lambda-cyhalothrin.

AGR-THIAMX-TC.note: A chlorinated thiazole-based intermediate is condensed to close the oxadiazinane ring characteristic of thiamethoxam, a second-generation neonicotinoid insecticide.

AGR-PARAQ-TC.note: Pyridine (built up from formaldehyde/acetaldehyde chemistry) is reductively coupled to form 4,4'-bipyridyl, which is then quaternized on both nitrogens with methyl chloride to give paraquat dichloride.

CTG-DISP-LIQ.note: Acrylic acid is free-radically copolymerized with maleic anhydride in aqueous solution to build a low-molecular-weight polyelectrolyte backbone, then neutralized with caustic soda to the sodium salt — the same general comb/polyelectrolyte chemistry family as polycarboxylate superplasticizers, tuned here to a shorter chain length and higher carboxylate density for pigment-surface adsorption rather than cement-particle dispersion.

CTG-DEFM-LIQ.reaction: Mechanical emulsification (physical process, not a chemical synthesis)
CTG-DEFM-LIQ.note: Hydrophobic fumed silica particles are dispersed into a mineral oil carrier, then the oil phase is emulsified into water using a fatty alcohol ethoxylate emulsifier — a physical blending/emulsification process rather than a chemical reaction; the silica particles are the active defoaming agent, destabilizing foam lamellae on contact, with the oil acting as the carrier/spreading vehicle.

AGR-TSPE-LIQ.note: Phenol is alkylated with three moles of styrene under acid catalysis (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) to build the tristyrylphenol hydrophobe, which is then ethoxylated with ethylene oxide under base catalysis to add the hydrophilic polyether chain — the same general alkylation-then-ethoxylation chemistry family as nonylphenol ethoxylates, but using styrene rather than a linear alkene, giving TSPE a bulkier, more chemically distinct hydrophobe with different regulatory standing than NPE.

SUR-AMPHO-LIQ.note: Coconut fatty acid is condensed with aminoethylethanolamine (AEEA) to form a cyclic imidazoline intermediate, which is then ring-opened and carboxymethylated with one or two moles of sodium monochloroacetate (neutralized with caustic soda) to give the mono- or di-carboxylate amphoacetate — a related but distinct route from betaine (CAPB) synthesis, which quaternizes an open-chain amido-amine directly rather than ring-opening a cyclic imidazoline.

AGR-DBE-LIQ.note: The mixed diacid byproduct stream generated during adipic acid production (glutaric and succinic acids alongside the main adipic acid product) is esterified with methanol to give a blend of dimethyl esters — a byproduct-valorization route that gives this solvent a genuinely different economic logic than a dedicated single-feedstock solvent.

SUR-EOPO-LIQ.note: Ethylene oxide and propylene oxide are sequentially block-copolymerized onto a low-molecular-weight starter (e.g. propylene glycol) under base catalysis, building alternating hydrophilic (EO) and hydrophobic (PO) blocks whose ratio and arrangement tune the final HLB and surfactant properties.

MIN-CNSX-LIQ.note: Bis(2,4,4-trimethylpentyl)phosphinic acid is synthesized by free-radical addition of hypophosphorous acid to diisobutylene (two sequential additions to give the dialkylphosphinic acid), or via a Grignard route from PCl3. The resulting dialkylphosphinous acid is oxidized to the phosphinic acid. Syensqo's proprietary manufacturing process (ex-Cytec) at Niagara Falls uses an optimized continuous process; Chinese generics use batch methods with lower purity. Dissolved in kerosene for commercial use.

MIN-CUSX-LIQ.note: Nonylphenol is carboxylated (Kolbe–Schmitt or Duff reaction) to give 2-hydroxy-5-nonylbenzaldehyde (the salicylaldehyde), which is then reacted with hydroxylamine to form the aldoxime active ingredient. Ketoxime variants (LIX 84-I) use acetophenone oximation instead. The active oxime is dissolved in a high-flash-point kerosene diluent and blended with proprietary modifiers (esters, alcohols) to tune extraction–stripping kinetics. Formulation know-how and modifier chemistry are the key IP, not the oxime synthesis itself.

F27-VAN-PWD.note: The dominant industrial route: phenol is hydroxylated to catechol (H₂O₂/acid catalyst), catechol is O-methylated with methanol to guaiacol, then guaiacol is condensed with glyoxylic acid (electrophilic aromatic substitution at the para-position to the phenol –OH) to form vanillylmandelic acid, which undergoes Cu-catalyzed oxidative decarboxylation to yield vanillin. Alternative routes: Borregaard's lignin oxidation process (alkaline CuO-catalyzed oxidative cleavage of softwood lignin, producing vanillin as a primary aromatic fragment); bio-based ferulic acid bioconversion (enzymatic or microbial decarboxylation of ferulic acid from rice bran).

BCI-TEA-LIQ.note: Three sequential ethoxylations of ammonia: NH₃ + 3 EO → TEA. Co-produced with MEA and DEA in all ethanolamine plants. The product ratio favors TEA when the EO:NH₃ molar ratio is >3:1.

BCI-DEA-LIQ.note: NH₃ + EO → MEA (monoethanolamine); MEA + EO → DEA (diethanolamine); DEA + EO → TEA (triethanolamine). All three are co-produced; the product ratio is controlled by the EO:NH₃ molar ratio and recycle strategy. Higher EO:NH₃ ratios favor TEA; lower ratios favor MEA.

BCI-2EH-LIQ.note: Propylene + syngas → n-butyraldehyde (Co or Rh-catalyzed hydroformylation), then 2 mol n-butyraldehyde → 2-ethylhexenal (aldol condensation, NaOH catalyst), then hydrogenation (Ni catalyst) → 2-ethylhexanol. The Rh-catalyzed low-pressure oxo process (LP-OXO, licensed by Dow/Johnson Matthey) is now dominant over the older Co-catalyzed high-pressure route.

BCI-ACRYL-LIQ.note: Modern route: ACN + H₂O → acrylamide, catalyzed by nitrile hydratase enzyme (from Rhodococcus rhodochrous) at ambient temperature. Achieves >99.9% selectivity. Older chemical route used Cu catalyst at 70-120°C with lower selectivity. The enzymatic route is now dominant globally due to energy savings and purity advantage.

BCI-CACL2-LIQ.reaction: HCl + limestone neutralization / Natural brine extraction
BCI-CACL2-LIQ.note: Chemical route: 2HCl + CaCO₃ → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. The HCl is typically a chlor-alkali or organic chlorination byproduct. Natural brine route: underground CaCl₂-rich brine (from ancient evaporite deposits) is pumped and concentrated by solar or mechanical evaporation. Solvay process co-product route: CaCl₂ is formed as a waste stream from Na₂CO₃ production.

BCI-NAPH-LIQ.note: Naphtha is obtained as a straight-run cut from atmospheric distillation of crude oil (boiling range ~30-200°C). Light naphtha (C5-C6, IBP-70°C) is used for isomerization/gasoline; full-range naphtha (C5-C12) feeds steam crackers; heavy naphtha (70-200°C) feeds catalytic reformers for BTX/gasoline. Not a synthesis product — it is a physical separation from crude.

BCI-PRP-GAS.reaction: Steam cracking co-product / FCC co-product / Propane dehydrogenation (PDH)
BCI-PRP-GAS.note: Three main routes: (1) steam cracker co-product from naphtha cracking (~30% of feed becomes propylene); (2) FCC refinery co-product (~5% of crude feed); (3) on-purpose PDH — catalytic dehydrogenation of propane (Oleflex or CATOFIN process) at 550-700°C over Pt or CrOx catalyst. China's PDH boom uses imported US/ME propane.

BCI-ETH-GAS.note: Hydrocarbon feed (naphtha or ethane) is mixed with steam and heated to 750-900°C in tubular furnaces for milliseconds, causing thermal cracking into ethylene, propylene, butadiene, and BTX co-products. The product mix depends heavily on feed: ethane crackers yield ~80% ethylene; naphtha crackers yield ~30% ethylene with significant propylene, C4, and aromatics co-products.

BCI-BDO-LIQ.note: The classical BASF Reppe route: acetylene and formaldehyde undergo ethynylation (Cu-acetylide catalyst) to form 2-butyne-1,4-diol, then hydrogenation (Ni catalyst) to BDO. Alternative: Dairen/LyondellBasell route via allyl alcohol (from propylene oxide isomerization) + hydroformylation. Chinese producers use coal-to-acetylene (CaC₂ route) feeding the same Reppe chemistry.

BCI-CL2-GAS.note: Saturated NaCl brine is fed to membrane cells where electrolysis splits NaCl + H₂O into Cl₂ (anode), NaOH + H₂ (cathode). Modern plants use ion-exchange membrane technology (replacing mercury and diaphragm cells). The fixed ECU ratio means chlorine cannot be produced without co-producing caustic soda.
